subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable Agent Bundles be a first-class core CLI/RPC feature, a new generic plugin/ClawHub bundle API, or out of scope for now?
rationale: Current main has adjacent manual agent, workspace, skill, routing, and bundle-plugin pieces, but no maintainer-approved contract for safely packaging and restoring an existing agent across config, workspace, binding, skill, secret, and runtime-state boundaries.

options.title: Design core bundle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open for a core-owned export/import manifest, dry-run importer, explicit non-secret allowlist, overwrite semantics, and focused security review.

options.title: Move to plugin API design
options.body: Narrow this into a generic plugin/ClawHub bundle API gap if maintainers want portable agents distributed as installable packages rather than core commands.

options.title: Decline for now
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide workspace Git plus manual config and skill install steps are the intended portability path for the current roadmap.

recommendation.title: Design core bundle contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a core-owned export/import manifest, dry-run importer, explicit non-secret allowlist, overwrite semantics, and focused security review.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily product/core-boundary and security posture, and steipete is the strongest available routing signal from VISION and recent adjacent agent/gateway history.
